variants.headline: Party divides in two
variants.sub: The colony has seen a party divide into two organisations.
variants.body:
A political party has split in two in {colony}. The division is an organisational fact, not a complete explanation of the differences behind it. In considering {target}, readers should distinguish the break itself from unreported motives, ideological labels or claims about the balance of parliamentary strength.

Political unity has value when it enables common convictions to act. It is not a principle that can settle every disagreement by itself. Our movement should judge a division by the commitments at stake, rather than granting either unity or separation an automatic claim to righteousness in every case.

We judge {target} harshly in this matter. Political organisation carries obligations beyond the comfort of its leaders, and division is an appropriate occasion to question the quality of that stewardship. Political principle should remain visible when judgment becomes less comfortable.
